purpose: D-025 author confirms no drilling; replace unsupported wall mounting with own floor frame in all four panels
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied complete 2x2 industrial design sketch sheet. Preserve its four panels, same people, same exercise poses, same warm brown and gray pen/pencil sketch style, same central folding seat, storage layout, dumbbells and single floor pad. No text or numbers.
IMPORTANT CHANGE IN ALL FOUR PANELS: the product must now be FREESTANDING ON THE FLOOR with NO attachment, leaning, bearing or fixing to any wall. Turn the formerly floating wall panel into a slim FLOOR-STANDING STORAGE CONSOLE near a wall. Add continuous clearly visible structural vertical side members down to the floor, connected to a SUBSTANTIAL WIDE FLOOR PLINTH. Show sufficient front-to-back depth of its base in three-quarter perspective, with wide left and right floor feet or plinth ends. The support must be visibly the same in every panel and physically connected to cabinet, no floating parts or unsupported hanging box. Keep clear the older woman's feet and the child's floor mat. The wall behind is only a faint background outline with an obvious small visual air gap, NOT the product's support. Absolutely no wall fasteners, no adhesive pads, no pressure poles, no ceiling attachment, no bolts through the room.
TOP LEFT: the closed product stands on its floor base, with two structural side supports reaching floor. TOP RIGHT: same floor base and support structure, seat unfolded and older woman seated as before, two existing separate front seat-support legs still clearly reach the floor left and right beyond her shoes. The rear seat load goes to the freestanding cabinet frame, not wall. BOTTOM LEFT: child and adult as before, unfolded floor pad in front and storage sleeve empty, same support structure reaches floor. BOTTOM RIGHT: young man returning dumbbells as before, same cabinet on same connected floor base, floor pad folded in sleeve. Do not add more exercise equipment, wheels, people, extra limbs or second mats. Preserve white margins and make the structural change understandable as a preliminary design hypothesis; do not imply proven stability or safety.
limits: Concept illustration only; stability and load paths require later calculation and physical verification.
